newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan sees improvement in second half.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan sees improvement in second half.

text.p: Donna Karan International Inc on Wednesday said it expected its cost-containment plan to pay off during the latter part of the year, with its bottom line improving in the second half.
Stephen Ruzow, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement that cost-cutting was one of the fashion design company's highest priorities.
"We are finalizing specific actions to meet these objectives, which we expect to announce by the end of the month," he said.
A company spokeswoman declined to provide details about its cost-reduction plans.

Earlier, Donna Karan said first-quarter net income fell to $806,000 or $0.04 a share, from pro forma net income of $6.2 million, or $0.29, in the comparable period of 1996. Revenues dipped to $158.8 million from $159.6 million.
Pro forma 1996 results assume the company's initial public offering, which closed on July 3, 1996, had been completed on the first day of the year.

The company said its first-quarter results reflected a shift of some spring shipments to the second quarter and a decreased focus on its jeans business. There were also delayed shipments and cancelled orders because of production difficulties in the Donna Karan New York women's collection.
"We are disappointed with out first-quarter results," said Donna Karan, chairman and chief executive officer, but she added the results did "not reflect our future performance."
She said the company's international division was still providing support, generating 37 percent of sales in the first quarter.
In March, the company terminated its jeans licensing agreement with Designer Holdings Ltd and agreed to return a $6 million payment and a $1.26 million advance royalty payment.
Karan said retail customers had favorably received the company's decision to bring its jeans line in-house.
